newsitem.title: USA: Federal Express sees Latam hub in Miami.
newsitem.headline: Federal Express sees Latam hub in Miami.

text.p: Federal Express Corp expects to create a Latin American hub in Miami within two years and add a hub in Latin America later, a FedEx official said Monday.

"We believe we will create a Latin American hub within the next two years in Miami," Joseph McCarty, FedEx's vice president Latin American and Caribbean division, said. "That will give us connectivity to our European and Asian express freight networks."
FedEx's current flight and sorting hub for Latin America is at its headquarters in Memphis, Tennessee, McCarty said.

"Eventually we will have a Latin American hub down there ... probably in the northern part of the hemisphere," somewhere between Panama or Caracas, McCarty told more than 300 industry executives attending the International Airline CEO conference, organized by Aviation Management Services and run by consultant Robert Booth."The volumes have not developed enough for this yet," he said.
McCarty said he will work for open skies for cargo in Latin America.

"I'm hoping to work in this part of the world, like I have others to bring the notion of deregulation for air cargo," he said. "All of us ought to be working for the deregulation of air cargo," he said.

Asked about the difficulty of delivering time-sensitive goods in Latin America, McCarty said "the single greatest problem with time sensitive delivery throughout the world is customs. The customs barriers in Latin America are not unique."
FedEx has installed a system in Chile "that is as sophisticated as anything in Asia" and he said Brazil is close behind with a similar FedEx system.

FedEx has gotten sidetracked in Colombia with aviation agreement problems but "within the next six months, I believe we will have direct service. There is pressure from our global customers, especially in auto and telecommunications," he said.
